subject: chemistry-1
question: Butane undergoes complete combustion according to the unbalanced equation C4H10 + O2 -> CO2 + H2O. When the equation is balanced with the smallest possible whole-number coefficients, what is the sum of all four coefficients?
explanation:
Balancing carbon and hydrogen first gives C4H10 + 13/2 O2 -> 4 CO2 + 5 H2O, and multiplying every coefficient by 2 clears the fraction to give 2 C4H10 + 13 O2 -> 8 CO2 + 10 H2O, so the coefficients sum to 2 + 13 + 8 + 10 = 33. The atom inventory confirms 8 C, 20 H, and 26 O on each side, since 13 x 2 = 26 and (8 x 2) + 10 = 26. The sums 24 and 29 arise from doubling only some of the coefficients after clearing the fraction (24 = 2 + 13 + 4 + 5 and 29 = 2 + 13 + 4 + 10), while 31 is simply a nearby total that no correct balancing produces.

ELI-10: Balance carbon and hydrogen first because each appears in only one product, and leave oxygen for last because it appears in two. That gives 4 CO2 and 5 H2O, which need 13 oxygen atoms, or 6.5 O2 molecules. Since half a molecule is not allowed, multiply every coefficient in the equation by 2, exactly as you would double a whole recipe rather than one ingredient. The result is 2, 13, 8, 10, which adds to 33.
source: OpenStax — Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e); NIST — Reference Data / Constants (https://www.nist.gov/pml)
